source: NCERT Class XI, Statistics for Economics, Ch. 3 (Organisation of Data).

sections.heading: 1. Classification of Data
points: **Raw data** collected must be **organised (classified)** to make it useful.
**Classification** = arranging data into groups/classes according to common characteristics.

sub: **Chronological** (by time), **Spatial/Geographical** (by place), **Qualitative** (by attributes like gender), **Quantitative** (by numerical value like income).

sections.heading: 2. Variables and Frequency Distribution
points: A **variable** = a characteristic that can take different values; **discrete** (whole numbers, e.g. number of children) or **continuous** (any value in a range, e.g. height).
**Frequency** = the number of times a value occurs.
A **frequency distribution** classifies data into classes with their frequencies.

sections.heading: 3. Class Intervals and Types
points: A **class interval** has **lower and upper limits**; **class width = upper − lower limit**; **mid-value (class mark) = (upper + lower)/2**.
**Exclusive method** — the upper limit of one class = lower limit of next (upper limit excluded); used for continuous data.
**Inclusive method** — both limits included in the class (a gap between classes; needs correction for continuity).
**Frequency** can be shown as simple, cumulative (less than / more than), and relative frequency.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Classification bases: chronological, spatial, qualitative, quantitative.
Variable = discrete (whole values) or continuous (any value).
Frequency = number of occurrences; frequency distribution = classes + frequencies.
Class mark (mid-value) = (upper + lower limit)/2; class width = upper − lower.
Exclusive method (upper limit excluded) vs Inclusive method (both included).

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Discrete variable = whole numbers**; **continuous variable = any value in a range**.
In the **exclusive method** the **upper limit is excluded** from the class.
**Classification** groups data by common characteristics (time, place, attribute, value).
